about: The epistola of the formulary “Third Sunday after Epiphany” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: Do not be wise in your own estimation. Repay no one evil for evil; take care to do what is good not only before God but also before all men. If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, have peace with all men. Do not avenge yourselves, dearly beloved, but give place to wrath; for it is written: Vengeance is Mine, I will repay, says the Lord. But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head. Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

a.g: repay no one evil for evil
take care to do what is good
as far as it depends on you
you will heap coals of fire

ex.w037: Defendentes is an active nominative plural participle. Here, beside Mihi vindicta and the command to feed an enemy, it concerns taking personal vengeance into one’s own hands. The English exhortation does not turn the Latin participle into an imperative or impose a universal prohibition of defense.
